A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Old Nepali handwriting-recognition study. All 27 pages of each version, including Appendices A–S, support comparison; relocated tables and retained figure contents can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original model comparisons, augmentation ablations, recognition benchmarks, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds metric entries and diagnostic results from splitting long lines.

M1.justification: The three-stage training pipeline, architectures, tokenizers, normalization, augmentation, and decoding methods remain unchanged. Long-line splitting is presented as a diagnostic experiment; v2 does not report incorporating it into the recognition pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic corpus, 5,139 printed Devanagari lines, and 3,100 Old Nepali lines from 155 manuscripts. The new splitting experiment changes preprocessing of existing long-line cases within the retained task.

E2.justification: Fine-tuned TrOCR, Google Cloud Vision, and the architecture, decoder, tokenizer, and decoding comparators are retained. Min-k is newly cited but not evaluated. Removing 'small' from the encoder-size table caption does not remove a comparator: both versions contain only base and large rows there.

E3.justification: V2 adds reevaluation after splitting long lines into two parts. Table 3 revises the reported 16× augmentation sample count from 32,240 to 42,160. Sections 4.1 and 5.5 correct Adam to AdamW and validation to test, agreeing with v1's appendix and Figure 11. These reporting corrections do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V1 already analyzes errors versus line length. V2 Section 5.5 adds identification of scattered missing tokens and consecutive 3–7-character error segments, followed by a focused test of splitting long lines. The existing ablations and appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 42 and 36 configuration-stage training runs, without adding repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix P's token-uncertainty procedure and reporting also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds weighted CER entries to Table 3 and weighted CER and accuracy to the architecture comparison relocated from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 7. Section 5.5 newly reports errors falling from 23 to 4 and from 30 to 2 after splitting example lines. Existing CER results, including the headline 4.9%, are retained.

T1.justification: The CER and weighted-CER definitions in Equations 1–2 and the relative-probability ratio in Appendix P are mathematically unchanged. Revisions concern notation and explanation; no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the pipeline and 4.9% CER claims. The conclusion narrows robustness across line lengths to short-to-medium lines and qualifies the advantage of data-centric improvements as applying in this context.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the splitting examples as evidence of difficulty handling long sequences and a possible remedy. It additionally explains that absent word boundaries complicate post-correction and mentions rare character combinations as a limitation. Existing data-access, generalization, and segmentation limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents randomized font and augmentation selection for synthetic images, explicitly identifies CER as the model-selection criterion, and supplies a URL for the existing web application. The font lists, augmentation parameters, hardware, and training hyperparameters were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Ding et al. (2026) on Min-k sampling to the decoding literature. The broader related-work coverage and positioning of the contribution remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits mainly correct grammar, terminology, repetition, and cross-references, with localized rewriting of the error analysis and expansion of the conclusion. Appendix headings are revised, while the main section sequence and narrative organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The architecture comparison moves to Appendix C, while training hyperparameters and the encoder-size comparison move into the main text. Tables gain metric columns and revised formatting, highlighting, and captions. Figures retain the same underlying images and plots, with limited caption and placement changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and internal consistency through corrected sample counts, optimizer and evaluation-set descriptions, fuller metric reporting, and an application link. Its focused long-line diagnostics and narrower robustness claim better explain the existing failure boundary. These are useful but limited gains: the added diagnostic evidence consists of selected examples, and the principal experimental conclusions remain unchanged.
